articles.titleCn: 数字创新为亚太互联互通搭建新基地

articles.fullText:
Digital innovation is emerging as a key driver of growth across the Asia-Pacific, offering new ways to strengthen regional connectivity, narrow development gaps and promote inclusive growth.
Cooperation in areas such as satellite technology, cross-border data flows, digital trade and artificial intelligence (AI) is helping to build a more connected and prosperous Asia-Pacific community.
Satellite technology strengthens disaster resilience
A BeiDou-based autonomous driving system for agricultural machinery displayed at the 2026 China International Industry Fair, Shanghai, China, October 13, 2026. 
China's BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) is evolving from a positioning and navigation tool into a broader digital infrastructure platform.
The annual report on the development of the BDS industry released in September suggested that the industry applications will increasingly combine satellite navigation with technologies such as 5G, the Internet of Things, AI, remote sensing, inertial navigation and visual perception to deliver integrated solutions for different sectors.
So far, BeiDou products have reached more than 140 countries and regions, with a market share of 58% in the Belt and Road partner countries. The system has also been incorporated into the standards of 11 international organizations, including the International Civil Aviation Organization and the International Maritime Organization.
BeiDou-empowered solutions are yielding practical results across the Asia-Pacific region. In Pakistan, a BeiDou-based flood early-warning system covers 80% of the country's flood-prone areas and provides up to six hours of advance warning, according to Ahsan Iqbal, Pakistan's minister of planning, development and special initiatives. Precision agriculture technologies have also helped increase wheat yields by 15%, while smart transport systems have helped ease congestion in major cities such as Karachi.
In Mongolia, pilot applications of BeiDou-based satellite livestock tracking are helping improve real-time animal positioning and emergency assistance in remote areas. Integrated with weather monitoring equipment, the technology can also support more accurate warnings of extreme weather.
New models for cross-border data cooperation
The Songshan Lake Science City, a core innovation and high-tech hub in Dongguan, south China's Guangdong Province. 
As digital trade expands, the ability to move data securely and efficiently across borders is becoming increasingly important.
In August, Guangzhou, Shenzhen and the Guangdong-Macao In-Depth Cooperation Zone in Hengqin were selected as China's first batch of pilot sites for international cooperation in the data sector, with support from the National Data Administration. The initiative marks a new step in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area as a hub for cross-border data cooperation.
The three areas will leverage their respective strengths. Guangzhou plans to build an international data cooperation system integrating infrastructure, rules, platforms and ecosystems, with a focus on emerging digital sectors such as cross-border trade, autonomous systems, healthcare and connected intelligent vehicles. Shenzhen will focus on infrastructure connectivity, mutual recognition of standards, development of cooperation platforms, and cultivation of service ecosystems, with an aim to overcome institutional and technical barriers to cross-border data flows and foster new types of data services for global markets. Hengqin, leveraging its links with Macao Special Administrative Region, will explore cooperation with Portuguese- and Spanish-speaking countries to establish new hubs and channels for international data cooperation.
In September, the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region and Nansha District in south China's Guangzhou City launched a sandbox cooperation mechanism for the low-altitude economy. The initiative will test rules, standards, technologies and applications, with the longer-term goal of extending cooperation to autonomous vehicles and vessels, supporting the Greater Bay Area in building a world-class industrial cluster for integrated autonomous systems across land, sea and air.
Digital services facilitating channels
The Shenzhen International Business e-Station, Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, August 10, 2026. 
Digital connectivity is also making it easier for small- and medium-sized enterprises to participate in regional supply chains.
In Shenzhen, the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone is developing an integrated supply chain service platform to help companies expand overseas. Through the "Shenzhen International Business e-Station," businesses can get full-chain support from market development and financing to intellectual property protection. The platform has established partnerships with 55 overseas industrial park operators in 32 countries and regions, with a focus on markets in APEC economies, including Malaysia, Vietnam and Mexico.
It has brought together more than 200 service providers and supported over 1,900 companies seeking to expand overseas, according to Liu Yang, head of the e-station.
A view of the Qianhai Shenzhen-Hong Kong Modern Service Industry Cooperation Zone, Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, October 18, 2026. 
Qianhai has also established Guangdong's first comprehensive service center for cross-border data flows, while a Shenzhen-Singapore cross-border data verification platform has entered trial operation.
At the APEC High-Level Forum on AI in July, China announced plans to establish a national center in Qianhai to promote cooperation on cross-border data flows among APEC economies.
The launch of the Action Initiative for Jointly Building Global Open Artificial Intelligence at the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, east China's Zhejiang Province, November 3, 2026. 
Meanwhile, China advocates for the open sharing of computing resources and works to coordinate the development of digital infrastructure.
At the 2026 World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit, the Action Initiative for Jointly Building Global Open Artificial Intelligence was launched. The initiative calls on countries to jointly develop and share computing resources and high-quality datasets, establish open-source seed funding, and support countries in the Global South in developing locally tailored AI applications.
"We hope to foster a more open global environment, a better governance framework and stronger security measures," said Wang Jian, member of the Chinese Academy of Engineering.
"From the perspective of open resources, we must ensure that even regions without these resources can benefit from the development of AI," said Wang.

articles.fullText:
China on Thursday called on the international community to find a home for the Secretariat of the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ Agreement) best positioned for its efficient operation, pointing out problems with the joint candidature by Belgium and Chile.
Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning made the remarks at a regular press briefing after Belgium and Chile on Nov. 6 announced the decision to join their candidatures for the seat of the secretariat. This joint candidature provides for the secretariat being based in the city of Valparaíso, Chile, the Clearing-House Mechanism (CHM) will be installed in and operating from Brussels, and Brussels will host the meetings of the subsidiary bodies.
Mao said that earlier this year, China nominated Xiamen to bid for the seat of the Secretariat of the BBNJ Agreement, noting that the candidature has quickly received the support of the majority of the Parties to the Agreement.
"By seeking an unauthorized backroom deal on issues that should be determined by the Conference of the Parties (COP), the joint candidature is problematic in at least six aspects," the spokesperson said.
First, it contravenes the stipulations of the BBNJ Agreement. According to the agreement, the seat of the secretariat, the specific modalities for the operation of the CHM, including its installation, as well as where the subsidiary bodies hold their meetings shall all be determined by COP, and the CHM shall be managed by the secretariat, she said.
"Belgium and Chile traded under the table what should be collectively determined by all Parties to the Agreement. This is a violation of the stipulations of the agreement and an act of disrespect to the authority of COP," Mao said.
Second, it contravenes procedural justice, Mao said, adding that the choice of the secretariat seat and the development of the CHM are two items of different nature scheduled to be collectively determined by COP through separate decisions.
The Belgium-Chile proposal bundles the two together in an attempt to force it as a package upon other Parties, which is against applicable procedural rules and a hijack of the Parties' will, she said.
Third, it contravenes established international practice. Stressing that the management of the CHM is a key mandate of the secretariat, Mao said in the practice established by other international treaties like the Convention on Biological Diversity, the secretariats and CHMs are located in the same place.
"The Belgium-Chile proposal, which locates the Secretariat and the CHM separately across the ocean, will without a doubt raise the operation cost, lower management efficiency, and increase the financial burden on the Parties to the Agreement," Mao said.
Fourth, it contravenes equitable geographical distribution. The vast majority of major global institutions are based in Europe, with none located in Asia. Developing countries have been calling on global institutions to redress this long-existing injustice and bring about greater fairness and equity, the spokesperson said.
She said Brussels is already home to the headquarters of NATO and the EU. "If this non-coastal city were to host the CHM of an ocean-related treaty as well, it would further widen the digital divide to the detriment of the shared interests of the Global South."
Fifth, it contravenes fair competition. Noting the BBNJ Secretariat is tasked with contributing to global ocean governance, and the selection of its seat should be a fair and friendly process in keeping with the rules, Mao said the Belgium-Chile proposal, however, politicizes the bidding process and attempts to divide Parties into camps.
"It not only undermines the principle of fair, friendly and healthy competition, but also negates the essence of multilateralism," she said.
Sixth, it contravenes the original commitment. Chile first made the bid citing its significance for the Global South. Yet according to the new proposal, Chile will no longer assume the substantive functions of the secretariat. Belgium, for its part, only seeks to host the CHM and thereby has in effect relinquished its bid for the secretariat seat, Mao said.
Stressing that the adoption and entry into force of the BBNJ Agreement is a victory of multilateralism, Mao said its implementation likewise needs to serve and advance the common well-being of all humanity.
"We call on the international community to find a home for the secretariat best positioned for its efficient operation and the effective implementation of the agreement," Mao said, adding that China firmly supports multilateralism and the cause of the UN, and is committed to promoting and improving global ocean governance.
She said that as one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement and the largest assessed-contributor to its budget, China has the will, capability and confidence to provide strong support and backing for the operation of the secretariat.
"China is full ready. We look forward to working with all Parties to the Agreement to keep the selection of the secretariat seat proceeding in the right direction, and uphold the overall and fundamental interests of the international community, especially those of developing countries," Mao said.

articles.summary: Climate change poses the biggest threat to the vision of ecological civilization, and no country can tackle the global challenge alone, said Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, on Thursday.

paragraphs.en: (ECNS) -- Climate change {{0}} the biggest threat to the vision of ecological civilization, and no country can {{1}} the global challenge alone, said Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, on Thursday. Süleyman Coşar, president of Türkiye's ÇEKUD environmental organization, made the remarks at the China-Türkiye Dialogue on Ecological Civilization and Green Transition held in Istanbul during the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31), which kicked off on Monday in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya. The dialogue was hosted by China News Service and the Research Center for Xi Jinping Thought on Ecological Civilization, with China News Network and the Policy Research Center for Environment and Economy of the Ministry of Ecology and Environment (PRCEE) as co-organizers. It's also the second multilateral event of China News Service’s flagship program "News Lounge" held in Türkiye. Coşar said ecological civilization is, in its broadest sense, a philosophical and political concept aimed at rebuilding the relationship between humanity and nature on the basis of balance and {{2}}, in response to the global climate crisis and ecological {{3}}.

paragraphs.en: He noted that discussions on ecological civilization, known in Chinese as "shengtai wenming," began in China in the 1980s. In 2018, the concept was {{4}} into China's Constitution as a national goal. Coşar outlined three key features of ecological civilization. First, it rejects a development model that treats humanity as the master of nature and seeks to protect life and {{5}}. Second, it places natural ecological assets and sustainability at the center of economic structures, moving beyond growth models focused primarily on GDP.
paragraphs.cn: 他指出，关于生态文明的讨论（中文称为“shengtai wenming”）于20世纪80年代在中国开始。2018年，这一理念被写入中国宪法，成为国家目标。科沙尔概述了生态文明的三个关键特征。第一，它拒绝将人类视为自然主宰的发展模式，力求保护生命和生物多样性。第二，它将自然生态资产和可持续性置于经济结构的中心，超越主要关注GDP的增长模式。

paragraphs.en: Third, it represents political and social transformation that {{6}} socialism with ecological principles, as reflected in China's national strategy. Addressing the challenges posed by climate change, Coşar said humanity's continued pursuit of a more comfortable lifestyle, along with industrial production, technological development, and warfare, has placed growing pressure on the environment and contributed to greenhouse gas emissions. He noted that while industrialization and technological progress have driven social development, they have also brought significant ecological challenges that should not be overlooked. The impact of warfare is particularly concerning. Beyond the direct destruction of natural environments and ecosystems, war-related activities also generate {{7}} emissions, with environmental {{12}} that may {{8}} for a long time and affect future generations.
paragraphs.cn: 第三，它代表了一种将社会主义与生态原则相结合的政治和社会变革，这体现在中国的国家战略中。在谈到气候变化带来的挑战时，科沙尔表示，人类持续追求更舒适的生活方式，加上工业生产、技术发展和战争，给环境带来越来越大的压力，并加剧了温室气体排放。他指出，虽然工业化和技术进步推动了社会发展，但也带来了不容忽视的重大生态挑战。战争的影响尤其令人担忧。除了对自然环境和生态系统的直接破坏外，与战争相关的活动还产生大量排放，其环境后果可能持续很长时间，并影响子孙后代。

Third, it represents political and social transformation that integrates socialism with ecological principles, as reflected in China's national strategy.

These systems enable full-process traceability and real-time monitoring of key stages, from concrete production to continuous-girder construction.

It will provide a convenient passenger transport link between western Inner Mongolia and northern Shaanxi and the Central, Southwest and South Central regions of China.

(ECNS) — China's renewable energy technology provides a real opportunity for the world to accelerate decarbonization, Laura Clarke, chief executive officer of ClientEarth, said during the 31st session of the Conference of the Parties to the U.N. Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31).
Speaking to China News Service on Tuesday at the China Pavilion, a side event of the COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, Clarke described China as "an extraordinary producer of renewable energy technology" and highlighted the potential for further cooperation on environmental protection.
Clarke praised China's continued progress in building an ecological civilization, saying it was "really remarkable" to see the advances made year after year.
Looking ahead, Clarke emphasized the importance of sharing "best practice and expertise" and said ClientEarth is interested in working with China on climate action.
She also pointed to opportunities for cooperation on green technology, while stressing that the transition must take environmental and social considerations into account.
On China's environmental achievements, Clarke said the country had made "real progress," with the law playing a significant role.
She highlighted China's system of environmental public interest litigation as a means of ensuring that environmental standards are properly implemented and enforced.
Clarke said ClientEarth has supported efforts to strengthen environmental enforcement, tackle pollution and protect nature.
She stressed that putting laws and regulations in place was only part of the solution and ensuring their effective implementation was equally important. In this regard, she pointed to the role of public interest environmental prosecutors and environmental courts.
On cooperation between developed and developing countries, Clarke called for stronger collaboration through trade agreements, the sharing of expertise and best practice, and mutual support in meeting environmental and climate commitments.
More than a decade after the Paris Agreement, she said, countries need to step up efforts to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, triple renewable energy capacity and electrify their economies.
She stressed that the energy transition must also protect nature, the environment and local communities, and be carried out "with and for people."
Recalling her visits to China, Clarke said attending the China Council for International Cooperation on Environment and Development, where Chinese and international experts discussed ways to achieve China's environmental and climate objectives.

（中新社）——地球客户组织首席执行官劳拉·克拉克在《联合国气候变化框架公约》第三十一次缔约方大会（COP31）期间表示，中国的可再生能源技术为世界加速脱碳提供了真正的机遇。周二，克拉克在土耳其安塔利亚举行的COP31边会中国馆接受中新社采访时，称中国是“非凡的可再生能源技术生产国”，并强调了在环境保护方面进一步合作的潜力。克拉克赞扬中国在建设生态文明方面持续取得的进展，称逐年看到的进步“确实令人瞩目”。展望未来，克拉克强调分享“最佳实践和专业知识”的重要性，并表示地球客户组织有兴趣与中国在气候行动方面开展合作。

她还指出了绿色技术方面的合作机遇，同时强调转型必须考虑环境和社会因素。关于中国的环境成就，克拉克表示中国取得了“真正的进展”，法律发挥了重要作用。她强调中国的环境公益诉讼制度是确保环境标准得到妥善实施和执行的手段。克拉克表示，地球客户组织支持加强环境执法、治理污染和保护自然的努力。她强调，制定法律法规只是解决方案的一部分，确保其有效实施同样重要。

在这方面，她指出了公益环境检察官和环境法院的作用。关于发达国家与发展中国家之间的合作，克拉克呼吁通过贸易协定、分享专业知识和最佳实践以及在履行环境和气候承诺方面相互支持来加强协作。她表示，在《巴黎协定》达成十多年后，各国需要加大力度减少对化石燃料的依赖，将可再生能源产能提高两倍，并实现经济电气化。她强调，能源转型还必须保护自然、环境和当地社区，并且要“与人民一起、为人民”进行。

回顾访华经历时，克拉克提到参加中国环境与发展国际合作委员会会议，会上中外专家讨论了中国实现环境和气候目标的方式。她表示，地球客户组织很高兴与中国当局和民间社会合作，并看到了在气候适应和韧性方面进一步合作的机会。
